notes:
Net map (the page is rotated ~22 deg, so every "vertical" rail runs down-right with slope dx/dy ~ 0.42; the inked area is only the band y=88..422, everything above and below is blank crop padding). Skeleton: a LEFT RAIL running from (90,88) at the top of the band down through (194,334) to a corner at (229,415) and on to (231,422) at the bottom of the band; a RIGHT RAIL running from a T at (350,270) down through a T at (387,358) and off the bottom of the band at (414,422); an UPPER BRANCH from the GND lead at (170,342) rising right through I-AC 3 to the T at (350,270); a LOWER BRANCH from the left-rail corner (229,415) rising right through capacitor 5 to the T at (387,358); and a series string resistor 0 -> inductor 2 hanging off the top, from (276,88) down to the T at (350,270).
0 = the left rail plus the grounded end of the upper branch: GND 4, the lower-left terminal of I-AC 3, the lower-left plate of capacitor 5, and the two off-band terminals inferred below (V-AC 1 left, resistor 6 left). n1 = the wire between the lower end of resistor 0 (~(310,163)) and the upper end of inductor 2 (~(315,185)) - a single clean diagonal, nothing else touches it. n2 = the stub above the band: upper lead of resistor 0 leaving at (276,88) plus one terminal of off-band V-AC 1. n3 = the right rail: lower lead of inductor 2, upper-right terminal of I-AC 3 (they meet at the T at (350,270), verified at 10x), the upper-right plate of capacitor 5 (T at (387,358), verified at 10x), and one terminal of off-band resistor 6. Electrically this is a one-node AC problem: V-AC + 20 kohm + 3 mH in series from ground to n3, with the 6cos10t A source, the 4 F capacitor and resistor 6 all in parallel from n3 back to ground.
Judgment calls: (a) KEY CALL - the crossing at (194,334), where the left rail and the ground lead/upper branch meet, is drawn as a plain X with NO junction dot and no hop (checked on a 1-px map and at 22x: the rail is continuous above and below, the branch is continuous left and right, the ink is only slightly thickened at the intersection). I nevertheless read it as a JUNCTION, on circuit sense: if it were a crossing, net 0 would consist of the GND symbol and the left terminal of current source I-AC 3 and nothing else, i.e. a current source with no return path, which the guide says is almost always wrong; and the whole rest of the circuit would then float. Reading it as a junction gives the textbook single-node network described above. The ground symbol sitting just left of a rail with its lead running onto that rail, with the branch continuing beyond, is standard drafting.
(b) OFF-BAND COMPONENTS - V-AC 1 (bbox centre (157,52)) and resistor 6 (bbox centre (337,482)) have bbox centres inside 512x512 but lie in the blank padding above/below the inked band, so neither symbol is drawn and neither can be traced. Exactly two wire ends leave the top of the band: the left rail at (90,88) and the upper lead of resistor 0 at (276,88); extrapolating both up the 0.42 slope to y=52 puts them at x~77 and x~261, whose midpoint (169) is close to V-AC 1's bbox centre x (157), so V-AC 1 bridges them: terminal 0 (left) = 0, terminal 1 (right) = n2. Exactly two wire ends leave the bottom of the band: the left rail at (231,422) and the right rail at (414,422); extrapolated to y=482 they sit at x~255 and x~439, midpoint 347, against resistor 6's bbox centre x of 337 - so resistor 6 bridges them: terminal 0 (left) = 0, terminal 1 (right) = n3. Both readings leave no wire end dangling.
(c) The third mark reaching the bottom of the band near x=306 is NOT a wire: a 2-px map of x 255-340 / y 380-424 shows it is the handwritten "4 F" value label under the capacitor (a "4" glyph with its cross-stroke at y=408), disconnected from the lower branch.
(d) The three long parallel diagonals at the far left ((3,84)->(144,420) and, further in, nothing), i.e. the extreme-left line (3,84)->(144,420) and the extreme-right line (366,84)->(504,420), carry no terminal anywhere in the frame; they are rails of the neighbouring drawings on the same page clipped in by the crop and get no net. The middle diagonal (90,88)->(231,422) is NOT an artifact: the GND lead, the upper branch and the lower branch all terminate exactly on it, so it is this circuit's ground rail.
(e) Terminal order: resistor 0 and inductor 2 are listed top-then-bottom as drawn; I-AC 3, capacitor 5, V-AC 1 and resistor 6 are listed lower-left-then-upper-right (i.e. left-then-right). Order does not affect any metric, and the +/- of V-AC 1 cannot be read because the symbol is not in the image.
